A wide horizontal editorial collage illustration made entirely of layered cut paper, framed for a 16:9 blog cover. One single soft light source from the upper left gives every paper layer a small, consistent cast shadow on the layer beneath it, and the paper has a subtle fibre texture.

One idea only: coffee harvest turning into a financial instrument, read left to right.
Left third: a Brazilian coffee hillside built from stacked paper ridges, with rows of coffee shrubs and a few red-and-green coffee cherries on the nearest branch, cut with straight knife edges.
Centre: the cherries and the terraced rows are cut into long paper strips that flow to the right like a conveyor belt, and the strips fold and stack into flat rectangular sheets — the moment of transformation, with the single lime accent used only here.
Right third: a calm, sober stack of certificate-like paper documents (the financial product), one sheet slightly fanned out, with a small round paper seal; no writing of any kind on the documents.

Composition: the transformation strip is the focal point in the centre; generous empty background at the top and bottom edges so the image can be cropped; a clear left-to-right reading path; no people, no coins, no bull or bear, no rising chart arrow.
